extracted.intended_audience: IP practitioners, patent attorneys, judges, and parties (domestic and foreign) involved in IP disputes in the Republic of Korea
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the court structure, jurisdictional allocation, and procedural features governing patent, trademark, design, utility model, copyright, and related IP disputes in the Republic of Korea. Explains administrative review (IPTAB), judicial routes, special courts/divisions, and practical rules affecting litigation strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative jurisdiction of the IPTAB
rubrics_metrics.description: The Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board (IPTAB) of the Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO) reviews administrative cases on patents, utility models, designs, and trademarks. Administrative cases include appeals from decisions of refusal by KIPO examiners, cases to invalidate registered rights or to confirm the scope of rights, and cases seeking correction (amendment) of specifications or drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial proceedings to revoke IPTAB decisions fall under the exclusive jurisdiction of the IP High Court of Korea. Administrative proceedings before the IPTAB are a separate administrative track and have their own remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial jurisdiction concentration for patent and related IP rights (post-2016)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since January 1, 2016, jurisdiction for disputes relating to 'patent and other IP rights (patents, utility models, designs, trademarks, and plant varieties)' is concentrated: first-instance civil lawsuits for these rights are heard exclusively by six designated district courts (Seoul Central, Daejeon, Busan, Daegu, Gwangju and Suwon), with Seoul Central having concurrent jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals from the main proceedings of these first-instance cases fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of the IP High Court of Korea. Appeals from preliminary injunction cases still go to the high courts. This concentration affects venue strategy and appeal routes for patent-related civil litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative vs. civil vs. criminal jurisdiction categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The framework distinguishes administrative jurisdiction (validity-related matters such as refusal, invalidation, confirmation of scope of rights, correction, cancellation), civil jurisdiction (civil infringement actions including damages, preliminary injunctions, permanent injunctions; civil copyright infringement), and criminal jurisdiction (criminal infringement of patent, trademark, copyright and design cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Which court and procedure applies depends on the nature of the claim (administrative challenge to register vs. civil enforcement vs. criminal prosecution). Some courts have exclusive jurisdiction over certain categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: District courts with exclusive first-instance jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Six district courts exercise exclusive jurisdiction for first-instance civil cases relating to patent and related IP rights: Daejeon, Busan, Daegu, Gwangju, Suwon and Seoul Central (with Seoul Central having concurrent jurisdiction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These designated district courts are the proper venues for filing first-instance civil IP suits in the concentrated jurisdiction regime; filing outside them risks improper venue issues and affects appeal paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals routing: main proceedings vs. preliminary injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals from the main proceedings in concentrated-jurisdiction cases go to the IP High Court of Korea, whereas appeals from preliminary injunction cases continue to be heard by the high courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Litigants should plan for different appellate tracks depending on whether a dispute concerns the main civil proceedings or interlocutory remedies like preliminary injunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and criminal IP cases follow ordinary tracks
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyright cases and criminal cases concerning patent, trademark or design rights are not subject to the jurisdictional concentration and follow regular civil and criminal procedures: these cases are filed with one of the 58 district courts in the first instance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For appeals: copyright cases are appealed to high courts, while criminal cases on patent, trademark, or design rights are appealed to appellate divisions of the district courts. The Supreme Court is the court of last resort in all cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of IPTAB administrative record and judicial litigation record
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative cases before the IPTAB and the revocation cases before the courts are not interlinked; arguments or evidence submitted to the IPTAB are not deemed as filed in the judicial proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must re-submit arguments and evidence when pursuing judicial revocation actions. This has evidentiary and tactical implications: materials relied on before IPTAB will need to be included anew in court filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: IP-specific procedural features: technical examiners and advisors
rubrics_metrics.description: The IP High Court of Korea and the Seoul Central District Court employ full-time technical examiners and maintain a pool of advisors in each technical field to support well-grounded, technically-informed judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of technical examiners/advisors improves the courts' capacity to handle complex technical evidence; parties should prepare clear technical presentation and consider expert evidence aligned to the court's technical resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Divisions and foreign-language procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The IP High Court and the Seoul Central District Court have International Divisions that allow parties to argue cases in a permitted foreign language, use court-provided interpretation services, or submit briefs and evidence in a foreign language without translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application to bring a case to the International Division may be filed when: a party is a foreigner or foreign company; there is a need to examine material evidence in a foreign language; or there are other circumstances with equivalent international implications. Mutual consent of the parties and permission by the International Division must be obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of online judgments and statistical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court and the IP High Court publish statistics and maintain online databases of judgments (links provided to the Supreme Court justice statistics page and the IP High Court decision database).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners can consult these online databases for recent figures, precedents, and statistical trends relevant to IP litigation in Korea. URLs are provided on the page for direct access.
